title: Colony and Vector
premise: Jude Whitlock, a low-caste terraformer on the forgotten colony of Meridian, tends a seed vault for settlers who will never arrive while the war between Earth and the colonies grinds on above him. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Jude discovers the flicker was a signal — an encrypted broadcast hidden in the planet's own mass, recorded by his dead predecessor and keyed to his genetic memory implants. Pursued by both fleets who want the message destroyed or weaponized, Jude must carry it to the relay at Meridian's core before Earth's final transmission loop seals the war's outcome forever. He delivers it: the message proves Earth abandoned the colony deliberately, and its release forces an armistice — but Jude, now carrying the memories of everyone the colony lost, chooses to stay behind as the living archive of what power tried to erase.
about_author: Cyrus Vane is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who maintain things — gardens, machines, lies — long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Seasons
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes daily life: he records logs for settlers who never came, tending the seed vault alone on near-abandoned Meridian. His quiet grief and routine are interrupted when his memory implant glitches with a fragment that isn't his. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; dust hangs, water rises, and every machine on the planet reboots. In the silence afterward, Jude's implant unlocks a buried message addressed to him by name from a woman he has no memory of meeting. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Predecessor Left Behind
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, intercut with recovered log entries from Dr. Ilsa Reyes, the terraformer whose memories were wiped into the colony archive. He learns she discovered the flicker pattern years ago and hid the decryption key inside the seed vault itself. Beat: obsession taking root.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Sera Okonkwo of the colonial fleet, ordered to investigate the anomaly. She lands at Jude's station under pretense of resupply but is hunting the signal. Their wary alliance forms over shared meals neither trusts. Beat: the first crack in Jude's invisibility.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Jude and Sera descend into the flooded sub-levels where Reyes hid her work. Jude experiences cascading memory bleed — Ilsa's life flooding into his — and realizes the 'message' is not data but testimony: proof Earth knew Meridian was dying and chose to let it. Beat: betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: Two Flags Over a Dead World
chapters.summary: Dual POV. An Earth vessel arrives demanding the signal; Sera's own command orders her to seize it for the colonial war effort. Both sides reveal they'd rather destroy the truth than lose the war. Jude realizes everyone wants him silent again. Beat: hunted, allies fracturing.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Lives
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The memory bleed threatens to erase his identity entirely; he can no longer tell which griefs are his. Sera, choosing her conscience over her orders, helps him stabilize using the garden's biometric cradle — the same tech meant for unborn colonists. Beat: identity crisis resolved through chosen connection.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The two race to the planetary relay at Meridian's core as Earth forces bombard the surface and colonial ships close in. Sera sacrifices her ship and career to buy Jude time, staying behind to jam pursuit. Beat: sacrifice, rising action cresting.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Inside the relay, with minutes left before Earth's loop locks permanently, Jude broadcasts Ilsa's testimony — and his own logs — to every ship in the system. Fleets go silent mid-engagement as soldiers hear the names of the abandoned. Beat: catharsis at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Colony and Vector
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, resolution. An armistice holds, fragile and ashamed. Offered rescue and reinstatement, Jude declines: someone must remain to tend the garden and remember. Now carrying the colony's full memory, he plants the first seeds meant for whoever comes next. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
